title: Responsiveness to transcranial magnetic stimulation for treatment of motor deficits after resection of supratentorial brain tumors
summary:
The motor areas of the cerebral cortex are significantly involved in the planning and execution of movements. Accordingly, damage to these areas, for example as a result of the surgical removal of a tumor in this area, can lead to significant motor impairments. Some scientists assume that these impairments are due to increased activity in the unaffected hemisphere of the brain. This initial compensatory process prevents the hemisphere of the brain damaged by the operation from regenerating. The aim of this study is to investigate whether non-invasive stimulation of the unaffected hemisphere can normalize the activity of the cerebral hemispheres and thus improve the rehabilitation of movement restrictions.
One method of non-invasive stimulation of the cerebral cortex is transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS). This involves applying a magnetic pulse to the cerebral cortex through the skull bone, which triggers a circumscribed current flow in the cerebral cortex (= induction current). As part of the study, the magnetic impulse can be applied specifically to the motor brain areas of the unaffected hemisphere with the aid of a navigation system. The application of a stimulus triggers slight movements of the fingers. In addition, the application of a series of stimuli attempts to temporarily inhibit the function of this hemisphere from the outside so that the damaged side is given more space to regenerate. Following this temporary inhibition, the affected muscles are then trained as part of regular physiotherapy.

interventions.name: Repetitive navigated transcranial magnetic stimulation (rnTMS) at 1 Hz for 15 minutes per session (900 pulses) for 7 days week-daily. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients after resection of a supratentorial brain tumor
- Deterioration of motor status immediately postoperatively compared to preoperative status
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Patients whose physical and mental condition allows them to give full and comprehensive informed consent
- Written declaration of consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients with contraindications for MRI imaging
- Patients with contraindications for a TMS examination
- >1 generalized seizure per week
- Pregnancy
- Age < 18 years
- Lack of consent to participate in the study
